title: Inquest into death of man shot in emergency ward
article: A coroner's inquest heard Tuesday that even though the black man who took a doctor hostage in the emergency ward of a Toronto hospital on New Year's Day last year was shot in a medical centre, it was unlikely that anyone could have saved his life.
Henry Masuka, 26, was killed by three gunshots after holding what looked like a gun to the head of a doctor and daring police to open fire. The gun was later found to be an unloaded pellet pistol.
"There were major arteries that were damaged, and the blood loss would have been extensive," said Dr. Sarah Keating, who performed the autopsy on Masuka's body the day after he died.
"With the gunshot wound to the back of the head, there was very extensive damage to the brain. He may well have not been able to be saved."
Keating said that Masuka also suffered major damage to his heart, liver, lungs and major arteries.
Witnesses said Masuka flew into a rage after hospital staff refused to treat his sick baby boy, telling him to take the child to a different hospital.
The two Emergency Task Force policemen who shot him were cleared of wrongdoing earlier this year by the province's police watchdog.
Masuka's family is suing police and the hospital, claiming that police handcuffed him and prevented physicians from attending to him immediately after he was shot.
John Masuka, Henry's father, said, "We are looking for justice to be done, not just for us, for Masuka, but for everybody in the country."

The inquest is expected to take about two weeks and hear from 25 witnesses. The jury will be asked to look at the police and hospital staff response and make recommendations avoiding another such tragedy.
